title: Ukrainian General Staff: 1,010 Russian Soldiers Killed or Wounded — Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,357,950
detail: Ukraine's General Staff reported on May 26, 2026 (Day 1,552 of Russia's full-scale invasion) that approximately 1,010 Russian soldiers were killed and wounded in the preceding 24 hours. Cumulative Russian military personnel losses since February 24, 2022 reached approximately 1,357,950. Equipment destroyed since the invasion: 11,954 tanks, 24,615 armored fighting vehicles, 42,751 artillery systems, 312,035 UAVs destroyed — including 1,790 drones taken down on May 26 alone. The sustained daily Russian casualty rate averaging 1,000+ in 2026 has brought cumulative 2026 losses past 141,500 (83,000+ irreversible per Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi). Russia launched 233+ combat engagements, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole axes.

media.caption: Ukrainian General Staff: 1,010 Russian soldiers killed or wounded May 26 — cumulative losses reach ~1,357,950 since Feb 24, 2022

title: Russia Strikes Mykolaiv with 122 Shahed Drones and 2 Iskander-M Missiles — Administrative and Residential Buildings Damaged
detail: Overnight into May 26, 2026, Russia launched 2 Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 122 Shahed/Geran-type loitering munitions toward Ukrainian territory. Mykolaiv in southern Ukraine was struck by drones, damaging one administrative building and two high-rise residential buildings. Ukrainian air defense intercepted the majority of the Shahed drones, but several penetrated defenses. Ukrainian intelligence warned of a planned large-scale combined missile and drone attack in the coming days. The attack continues Russia's pattern of overnight Shahed campaigns that have averaged 100–300 drones per night throughout May 2026. The preceding May 24 mass attack on Kyiv (600 drones + 90 missiles + Oreshnik hypersonic missile on Bila Tserkva) remains the largest single attack of the week. Meanwhile, Kaliningrad airport closed its airspace for the first time ever due to a Ukrainian drone threat.

media.caption: Russia launches 122 Shahed drones + 2 Iskander-M missiles overnight, hitting Mykolaiv residential buildings and admin infrastructure (May 26, 2026)

title: WFP Confirms Russian Iskander Missile Destroyed $1.4M Food Aid Warehouse in Dnipro — 130,000 People Affected; Second Strike on Same Facility
detail: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) confirmed on May 26, 2026 that a Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile had struck and destroyed its warehouse in Dnipro, eliminating $1.4 million worth of food aid intended to feed 130,000 people near the front line. This was the second time the same facility was hit — a drone previously struck it in November 2025. WFP Executive Director Cindy McCain called the strike 'Absolutely unacceptable.' Over 84 WFP-related incidents have been recorded in Ukraine in the past 18 months. The attack was part of a documented Russian pattern of targeting UN-marked humanitarian facilities, food distribution infrastructure, and supply convoys. Strikes on protected humanitarian assets constitute a war crime under Additional Protocol I of the Geneva Conventions. The Dnipro warehouse served communities near the contact line in Donetsk Oblast.

media.caption: Russian Iskander missile destroys WFP food warehouse in Dnipro — $1.4M food aid for 130,000 people destroyed in second strike on same facility (May 26, 2026)

title: Ukraine Strikes Belets Oil Depot in Bryansk Oblast — Fuel Supply to Russian Front Lines Disrupted
detail: On May 26, 2026, Ukrainian forces struck the Belets oil depot in Bryansk Oblast, Russia. The facility supplies fuel to Russian military units along the eastern and northern front lines, and its destruction is expected to complicate Russian logistics and fuel supply chains. Fires were also reported near a military airfield in Voronezh (southeastern Russia), with smoke visible from the facilities — consistent with additional Ukrainian long-range drone strikes. Ukraine's 2026 deep-strike energy infrastructure campaign has cost Russia an estimated $9+ billion in energy sector losses, targeting over a dozen refineries, oil terminals, and depots from Tuapse in the Krasnodar Krai to Kirishi in Leningrad Oblast. Ukraine's long-range drone campaign has also forced Russian authorities to restrict airspace over the Moscow air zone on multiple occasions.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes Belets oil depot in Bryansk Oblast — fuel supply to Russian front-line forces disrupted as deep-strike energy campaign continues (May 26, 2026)
